messages:
mira: Heads-up — noticed a regresssion (~12-18% per-token tail latency) on fp8 inference for long-history chat traffic after the recent calibration tweak. Spike shows up after ~40 tokens. Anyone else seeing this?
ajay: I saw a blip in daily perf dashboards around the same deploy window. Can you paste the per-token breakdown from the trace?
mira: Pasted CPU/GPU breakdown from the trace below (shortened):
```
per-token breakdown (p95): decode 3.8ms | kv_lookup 1.4ms | kernel_exec 7.2ms | kernel_launch_overhead 0.9ms | serialization 0.6ms
series shows kernel_exec jumping to 9-11ms at token 40+ for some seq lengths
```
sam_w: Do you have kernel counter totals? Curious if we transitioned to fallback kernels (int8/4bit) for some layers or sequence lengths.
katie: Also check KV cache hit-rate by prefix length — calibration changed dtype heuristics which might alter prefix-resident checks. If cache hit drops, more recompute and kernel launches happen.
mira: I captured the kernel counters and kv stats from the perf-trace run (1 minute window). Rough numbers:
```
window_tokens: 12.7k
kernel_launches_total: 1.14M
fp8_kernel_calls: 760k
int8_kernel_calls: 280k
4bit_kernel_calls: 0
kv_cache_hits: 68.4% (prev baseline ~81%)
batch_avg_size: 3.1 -> small dip to 2.5 on high-latency tails
```
mira: So it looks like (a) more int8 kernels are being selected on hot paths and (b) kv cache hit-rate dropped by ~12pp. That matches higher launch overhead and kernel_exec variance.
ajay: Interesting — more int8 kernels could be due to quantization calibration heuristics misclassifying some tensors as better served by int8 post-calibration. Did the calibration change thresholds?
mira: Yes — the last PR adjusted the quant-error threshold from 0.045 -> 0.038 for layerwise selection to favor smaller datatypes. That was intended to reduce memory but perhaps increased some costly conversions.
perf-bot: (profile-summary) detected increased kernel launch variance for model rw-13b-fp8-v2 between 1823400000..1823450000; trigger=kernel_launch_stddev>1.2ms.
sam_w: Two hypotheses: 1) calibration is pushing mixed-precision across layers causing extra dtype conversions that show as int8 kernel calls, 2) kv cache key hashing or shard placement for certain prompt patterns changed which reduces hit-rate. Both could be exacerbated by batching heuristics that now split prefixes differently.
katie: For observability, we need: per-layer kernel-type timeline, per-token kv_cache_hit boolean series, and per-request kernel_launch_count. Can we add counters in runtime to stamp: layer_i_dtype, dtype_conversion_count, per_token_kv_hit? Keep labels lightweight.
mira: I instrumented a quick run with added counters — small sample output:
```
request_id: r-45b3
tokens: 88
per_token_kernel_launches: [1,1,2,1,1,2,1,1,3, ...]
dtype_switches_total: 9
layers_with_int8: [3,4,9,10]
kv_hits_by_prefix_len: {0:100%,1:98%,8:83%,32:61%,64:41%}
```
ajay: That per-prefix breakdown is telling — big drop after 32 tokens. Could be cache shard expiry or a key format change. Any recent changes to kv key normalization?
mira: Not in code, but calibration PR touched the runtime's tensor-layout heuristics. Might be a side-effect where cache keys include a quantization tag now for some models (oops).
sam_w: Let's validate: run two experiments on canary nodes — A) revert quant-error threshold to 0.045; B) keep threshold but force no-key-tagging for kv cache. Measure p95 per-token and kv_hit. Short ramp (~30k tokens) should show differences.
katie: Also add microtrace labels to distinguish fp8->int8 fallback events. The trace should log "fallback_reason" at layer-level (low-precision->recompute, overflow correction, etc).
mira: I kicked off experiment A and B on a small canary. Early results (10k tokens):
```
baseline (calibrated 0.038): p95 token latency 13.2ms, kv_hit 68%
experiment A (threshold 0.045): p95 token latency 11.3ms, kv_hit 80%
experiment B (no kv quant-tag): p95 token latency 11.0ms, kv_hit 79%
```
mira: Looks like both reversing threshold and removing kv tag help; threshold has slightly larger effect. Suggests calibration threshold change caused both dtype selection and kv key divergence.
ajay: Action items: (1) revert threshold in next hotfix (owner: ajay) (2) patch runtime to avoid adding quant-tag to kv keys (owner: sam_w) (3) add per-layer fallback counters and per-request kernel_launch_count (owner: katie) (4) add a short dashboard tile showing kv_hit_by_prefix and dtype_mix by model (owner: mira).
katie: I can add the counters this afternoon; will make sure metrics are low-cardinality. Plan to roll metric as trace events + aggregated counters.
sam_w: I'll prepare the kv-tag patch and a small regression test that asserts stable keys across calibration changes.
perf-bot: (note) scheduled perf rollback job queued if p95 token latency >12ms in next deploy window.
mira: Thanks team — I'll watch canary and post a follow-up once hotfix is validated. :thumbsup:
